name: Mangelwurzel
family: Amaranthaceae, the amaranth family (formerly Chenopodiaceae, the goosefoot family)
grown_as: The mangold or mangel, a fodder beet grown for its very large root, traditionally for cattle and for Somerset mangold hurling. Drawn as an old red-orange 'Mammoth' type. Varieties can be orange-red, golden yellow, pinkish or white, and long or round. ⚠️ CHECK: William's variety and its root colour.
habit: Year 1: a large rosette of leaves 40 to 60 cm high from the top of a huge root, two-thirds or more of which stands above the soil like a barrel. Year 2: a leafy, branched flowering stem 1 to 1.5 m with long slender flower spikes.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette from the top of the root
leaf.outline: Large, oval to long oval, 20 to 40 cm long
leaf.base: Rounded to wedge-shaped, running a little down the stalk
leaf.veins: A broad pale midrib with side veins running towards the edge; veins pale green, cream or pinkish, not deep red as in beetroot
leaf.surface: Smooth, hairless, glossy, puckered between the veins
leaf.stalk: Thick, fleshy, broad, pale green, cream or flushed pink to red according to variety

flower.form: Tiny green petal-less flowers in small clusters along long slender spikes, as in beetroot
flower.petals: None: five small green fleshy segments curved over the centre
flower.behind: A small leafy bract under each cluster
flower.carried: In clusters of two to four along long branching spikes that form a loose plume
flower.size: Flowers 2 to 3 mm; spikes 20 to 50 cm
flower.season: June to August of the second year

fruit: Corky, knobbly brown seed clusters 4 to 6 mm, each holding several seeds, along the dry brown spikes.
seedling: Two narrow oblong seed leaves on a reddish or pale stem; seedlings come up in small clumps from each corky cluster.
winter: Roots lifted and clamped before hard frost. A plant left to flower overwinters as a small rosette on the root top.

leaf: one large simple oval leaf, untoothed and wavy
a thick pale or pinkish fleshy stalk and pale midrib
bloom: tiny green flowers with no petals in small clusters
clusters spaced along a slender spike
seed: a corky, knobbly, irregular brown lump
young: a rosette of large oval leaves on thick pale stalks
the root top starting to swell above the soil
crop: a very large barrel- or tankard-shaped root, most of it standing above the soil
orange-red skin above, paler where it was underground
a big rosette of leaves from the top, a thin tail root below
flower: a tall leafy stem with long slender green flower spikes
seedhead: dry brown spikes lined with corky seed clusters

look_alikes: Beetroot is the same species with a smaller, round, deep red root and red-veined leaves. Sugar beet has a white, cone-shaped root mostly underground. Swede has grey-green lobed leaves and a neck of leaf scars.
